changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.31[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Ready for Kodi 22 Piers RC2[/COLOR]
-Checked against the Kodi 22 RC2 source and Python 3.14: every Kodi function, setting, info label and skin tag luc_kodi uses is still there. Kodi 21 keeps working as before.
-While a Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HLG or HDR10 source plays, Kodi 22 skins can show its HDR type and Dolby Vision profile (8.1, 7, 5...). The profile is the one luc_kodi reads from the file, or the one in the release name when the file cannot be read.
-Python 3.14 rejects some valid server certificates that older Kodi accepted. If a Usenet server fails only for that reason, luc_kodi connects again with the previous rules; the certificate and the server name are still checked.
-The display test names Kodi's texture database without a version number (Textures14.db in Kodi 22).
[COLOR fffdb515]Daily and talk shows, in every service[/COLOR]
-Talk shows are often posted under the presenter's name: The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon comes as "Jimmy.Fallon.2026.09.21...". For shows that air daily, the presenter taken from the title (Jimmy Fallon, Seth Meyers, Stephen Colbert...) now counts as the show's name for every scraper and debrid service, always together with the exact air date.
-Torrentio, Comet, MediaFusion, Meteor, Peerflix, Sootio, TorrentsDB, Torz, Zilean and AIOStreams number these shows as IMDb does, which rarely matches TMDb (S14E08 on TMDb is S13E1408 on IMDb). luc_kodi now asks them for the episode that aired on that date, as Stremio's catalogue (Cinemeta) numbers it.
-Easynews, Knaben and The Pirate Bay also search "presenter + air date".
-Newznab asks the indexer by the show's TheTVDB ID and air date when the title finds nothing, and keeps only what the indexer says belongs to that show. Indexers without those IDs are searched by the presenter's name.
[COLOR fffdb515]Fixed[/COLOR]
-With skins that play trailers in the background (Nimbus and others), the source list or the search window could close on its own and cancel playback when the skin stopped its trailer. Stop no longer closes these two windows; Back still does.
-Trailers no longer start a subtitle search. They have no IMDb ID, so OpenSubtitles rejected every request.
-Leaving a Movies or TV Shows list before it finishes loading now stops its work at once, instead of fetching details in the background until Kodi had to force it to close.
-Library: luc_kodi folders are always written to the video database Kodi uses (it keeps the old ones after each update), the Movies folder uses Kodi's built-in TMDb movie scraper (the old one is no longer included, so films were not scanned; run the library setup again to fix a folder set up before), and paths with an apostrophe or quotes work.
-System status checks TheTVDB with the saved sign-in, as luc_kodi does, so a slow TheTVDB sign-in no longer shows as failed.
[COLOR fffdb515]Smoother Usenet playback[/COLOR]
-When a Usenet connection goes silent, the part of the video you are waiting for is asked for again on another connection after 3 seconds, and the first copy to arrive is used. Before, the picture could freeze for 10 seconds or more.
